findings.issue: FIX-2 last-owner guard has an open TOCTOU race (severity med, narrow window — NOT blocking per verifier directive). The guard reads 'is target an owner' + 'any OTHER active owner' inside a withTenantTx that uses a plain BEGIN = default READ COMMITTED, with NO SELECT..FOR UPDATE, NO SERIALIZABLE, NO advisory lock, and NO unique partial index. Worse, that read tx is SEPARATE from the later deactivation write (KC-first flow), so check and mutation are not even atomic. Concurrent scenario: two active owners A and B, two parallel PATCH{active:false} — one deactivating A, one deactivating B. Under READ COMMITTED each guard sees the other owner still active (the concurrent deactivation is uncommitted → invisible) → each counts >=1 other owner → both pass → both commit → tenant left with ZERO active owners. This is exactly the self-lockout brick FIX-2 was written to prevent, reachable only via simultaneous double-deactivation (uncommon admin op). The two db tests exercise only the serial path, so this window is untested and unblocked.
findings.suggestion: Follow-up (small task, founder to file): make the guard atomic — e.g. SELECT the OTHER active owners FOR UPDATE inside the SAME tx that performs the deactivation write, or run the guard+write under SERIALIZABLE with retry, or add a partial unique/count constraint enforcing >=1 active tenant-owner. Not required to land this fix; the primary security holes are closed and the serial guard is correct.
